approachQuestion.prompt:
Withdraw a Reservation

A finite acyclic singly linked list has n reservation nodes, each with value and next. Given head and k, remove exactly the kth node counted from the end (last is k=1) and return the new head. Preserve identities, values and relative order of survivors. Only next links may change; the removed node need not be freed or cleared. Constraints: 1 <= k <= n <= 200000. No length is supplied.

Input: A(8) -> B(3) -> C(9) -> null, k=3. Output: B -> C -> null.
Input: A(6) -> null, k=1. Output: null.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Use the fixed gap but start trailing at head without a sentinel and always bypass trailing.next.
options.feedback: When k=n the target is head; bypassing its successor cannot remove head.

options.text: Use a temporary sentinel before head. Advance lead k links from the sentinel, then move lead and trailing together until lead.next is null. Bypass trailing.next and return sentinel.next.
options.feedback: The fixed gap places trailing immediately before the target, including when it is the original head.

options.text: Store all node references in an array. Use its length to locate the target and predecessor, updating head if the target is first.
options.feedback: This locates the target correctly but retains every node reference although a fixed gap suffices.

options.text: Remove the kth node counted forward from head.
options.feedback: For A -> B -> C and k=1 this removes A instead of C.

details: Use a temporary sentinel before head. Advance lead k links from the sentinel, then move lead and trailing together until lead.next is null. Bypass trailing.next and return sentinel.next.
The sentinel makes removing the head use the same bypass as any other node. Keep a k-link gap, stopping lead at the last node so trailing points just before the victim, not at it.
